deviations.claim_in_article: “They enjoyed AI’s convenience, but a human was on the other end. They did not realize it.”
deviations.issue: This states as an actual user experience that users enjoyed the AI service and did not realize a human was handling the call. The Ledger reports a test without appropriate disclosure, but does not establish what users actually experienced or realized. The Japanese source presents this more as a conditional, illustrative scenario; the English wording makes it categorical.
deviations.explanation: The categorical claim about users’ actual experience is not established by the Ledger. It also strengthens the source’s conditional, illustrative wording into a definite claim, so changed_fact, changed_certainty, and unsupported_new_claim are true.
deviations.qualifier_text: Nearby: “might think”; “sometimes”; “If no one explained this clearly”
